outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no event settles or refutes Mazur's finiteness conjecture (Conjecture 3 of the 1992 paper) or the consequence that Z is not diophantine in Q. The union-of-components form (Conjecture 1) was refuted in 1997, before the window. Post-window events are a 2025 special case of the abelian-variety part (rank-1 elliptic curves over number fields in R), two 2024-2025 results on Hilbert's tenth problem over rings of integers (not Q), a neighbouring AI-lab manuscript claiming a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over Q (October 2026, unverified), and namesake results on other Mazur conjectures.
problem_asks: The Wikipedia bullet reads only 'Mazur's conjectures' (Topology section, frozen 26 Jan 2024 revision; no link; the live page's footnote cites Mazur, 'The topology of rational points', Experimental Mathematics 1 (1992) 35-45). Read from the statement, the bullet asks: (A) Mazur's union-of-components conjecture (Conjecture 1 in Poonen's numbering; the 1995 update restates it as: for a smooth variety V over Q with Zariski-dense V(Q), the closure of V(Q) in V(R) is a union of connected components of V(R), equivalently open in V(R)). (B) Mazur's finiteness conjecture (Conjecture 3 as cited by Cornelissen-Zahidi): for any variety V over Q, the closure of V(Q) in V(R) has only finitely many connected components. (C) Further conjectures of the 1992 paper that the bullet's plural may cover, not verified against the paper's text: a stronger homotopy-type statement (closure homeomorphic to the complement of a finite subcomplex in a finite complex, per secondary sources), and Conjecture 4 concerning elliptic pencils (per Gvirtz's citation). (D) The non-archimedean analogue (Mazur 1992, II.2; Cornelissen-Zahidi's Question 4.1): for a variety over a global field K and a valuation v, the Zariski closures of rational points near a point of V(K_v) form a finite family. (E) The consequence that Z is not diophantine over Q, which Cornelissen-Zahidi and Poonen derive from (B); Mazur's second conjecture in some sources. (F) The abelian-variety case: for a simple abelian variety A over Q of positive rank, the closure of A(Q) in A(R) contains the identity component A(R)^0 (per Waldschmidt and secondary sources; the 1992 paper's own wording was not read).

events.what_happened: Barry Mazur, 'The topology of rational points', Experimental Mathematics 1(1) (1992), 35-45, DOI 10.1080/10586458.1992.10504244. Poses the conjectures on the real topology of closures of rational points, the source the live Wikipedia footnote cites. It is the origin of problem_asks (A) to (D), not a result. Cornelissen-Zahidi cite its Conjecture 3 (finiteness); Poonen's essay identifies Conjecture 1 as the union-of-components question; Gvirtz cites its Conjecture 4 for elliptic pencils. The paper's text was not readable to me, so its own numbering is taken from these secondary citations.
events.delivers: No result. Records the statements of the conjectures; establishes nothing about their truth.
events.direction: Not a resolution. The statements assert that the closure is a union of components (Conjecture 1) and that it has finitely many components (Conjecture 3).

events.what_happened: Barry Mazur, 'Speculations about the topology of rational points: an up-date', Asterisque 228 (1995), 165-181 (Columbia seminar, 1992). Restates the union-of-components question for smooth V over Q with Zariski-dense V(Q): the closure of V(Q) in V(R) should be open in V(R). Discussion, no result. Known only from the Numdam abstract as quoted in a search summary and from Gvirtz's citation; the PDF was a scanned image and not readable to me.
events.delivers: No result. Restates the union-of-components question (A) in its open-subset form.
events.doubts: Text not read; the restatement comes from the abstract as quoted in a search summary and from Gvirtz's citation.
events.direction: Restates Conjecture 1's question; no direction taken.

events.what_happened: J.-L. Colliot-Thelene, A. N. Skorobogatov and P. Swinnerton-Dyer, 'Double fibres and double covers: paucity of rational points', Acta Arithmetica 79 (1997), 113-135. Cited by Gvirtz (2019) and Waldschmidt (1999) as the concrete counterexample to the union-of-components form: a smooth surface over Q whose Q-rational points are Zariski dense but whose closure in V(R) is not a union of connected components. Poonen's essay states Conjecture 1 'turned out to be no', citing this work. The Acta page I read shows metadata only; the paper itself was not read.
events.revisions: An MPIM preprint of the same authors (MPIM 1997 (42)) is listed for a different paper, 'Hasse principle for pencils of curves of genus one whose Jacobians have rational 2-division points' (Invent. Math. 134 (1998)); that paper's record mentions no Mazur conjecture.
events.delivers: Per the secondary sources: one smooth surface V over Q with Zariski-dense V(Q) whose closure in V(R) is not a union of connected components. This refutes the union-of-components form (A) as stated for all smooth varieties over Q. It does not decide the finiteness form (B), which Gvirtz's text does not mention and which Poonen's essay still lists as open.
events.remains: (B) finiteness of components over Q; (C); (D) over number fields; (E); (F). For (A), the special cases proved by others (Gvirtz) still hold.

checked_by.qualification: Arithmetic geometer working on Hilbert's tenth problem over Q and on Mazur's conjectures; wrote the survey of Mazur's work
checked_by.what_they_did: Reports the counterexample in his survey essay (Section 5, per its summary) and gives the answer to Conjecture 1 as 'no'. A citation, not an independent verification.

checked_by.qualification: Author of the 2019 Acta Arithmetica paper on Mazur's conjecture
checked_by.what_they_did: Cites the counterexample as established ('by a concrete counterexample [CTSSD97]') and states that it shows the conjecture fails without further assumptions on the variety.

events.directly_checkable: The surface is in the Acta paper, which was not read; the secondary sources give no equations.
events.doubts: Sources differ on which form is refuted. Poonen and Gvirtz treat the union-of-components form (A). A search summary said 'the general form has been refuted' without saying which form. Cornelissen-Zahidi say only that the stronger conjectures 'had to be slightly modified' after this counterexample. Gvirtz says refined versions 'have resisted attempts at disproving them'. The year is 1997 in the Acta record and in Gvirtz's citation; a search summary gave 1998 by pointing to the Inventiones paper above, which is about the Hasse principle and does not discuss Mazur.
events.direction: Cuts against the union-of-components form (A) for smooth surfaces over Q. Its stated content, as reported, does not touch the finiteness form (B).
events.object: Per secondary sources: a smooth surface over Q with Zariski-dense rational points whose closure in the real points is not a union of connected components. Explicit or non-constructive status not known; the construction (double fibres and double covers, per the Acta title) was not read.

events.what_happened: Michel Waldschmidt, 'Density measure of rational points on abelian varieties', Nagoya Mathematical Journal 155 (1999). Treats the abelian-variety part (F): for a simple abelian variety over Q of dimension d and Mordell-Weil rank at least d^2 - d + 1, the closure of A(Q) in the real topology contains A(R)^0, with an effective density statement. Not read: the PDF returned binary; the statement comes from search summaries and from the abstract of the 2025 Fishman et al. paper, which builds on Waldschmidt's work.
events.delivers: Per secondary sources: unconditional containment of A(R)^0 in the closure of A(Q) for simple A over Q under the rank hypothesis rank at least d^2 - d + 1. Not the general statement of (F).
events.remains: (F) for any rank below d^2 - d + 1; (A), (B), (D) and (E) for general varieties.
events.doubts: Paper not read. The threshold d^2 - d + 1 is taken from search summaries. One summary says a later talk states the bound as a strict inequality, so the boundary case differs between sources.
events.direction: Supports (F) under a rank hypothesis; does not settle (F).

events.what_happened: Gunther Cornelissen and Karim Zahidi, 'Topology of Diophantine sets: remarks on Mazur's conjectures', arXiv math/0006140 (submitted 20 June 2000; math.LO). States Mazur's Conjecture 3 (finitely many components for any V over Q; no counterexample known; some evidence). Shows that Conjecture 3 implies Z is not diophantine in Q. Gives a counterexample to the non-archimedean analogue (Question 4.1) over the function field F_q(t) with the valuation at t^(-1), built from Pheidas's and Videla's constructions. The paper's journal publication was not confirmed.
events.delivers: Conditional: Conjecture 3 implies Z is not diophantine in Q. Counterexample only for the non-archimedean analogue over function fields of positive characteristic. Nothing about Q or number fields.
events.remains: (B) over Q; (D) over number fields; (A) and (F) not addressed.
events.doubts: The conditional implication and the function-field counterexample are the authors' own. No independent reading was found.
events.direction: Uses (B) as a hypothesis. Refutes the non-archimedean analogue (D) in positive characteristic only.
events.object: In positive characteristic: a variety V over K = F_q(t) and the valuation at t^(-1) for which the answer to Question 4.1 is negative, using a space curve whose x-coordinates give the powers t^(p^s) (Pheidas, p > 2) or Videla's set (p = 2). Explicit, per the authors' account as reported; the paper was read only through its extracted statements.

events.what_happened: Dipendra Prasad, 'An analogue of a conjecture of Mazur: a question in Diophantine approximation on tori', arXiv math/0204359 (15 April 2002). For a torus T over Q and an arithmetic subgroup Gamma with Gamma\T(R) compact, shows under Schanuel's conjecture that closures of images of finitely generated subgroups of T(Q) are determined by subalgebraic tori. An analogue for tori, not Mazur's varieties.
events.delivers: Conditional (Schanuel's conjecture) result for tori. Analogue only.
events.doubts: Conditional on Schanuel's conjecture; no independent check.
events.direction: Analogue for tori; says nothing about the varieties in (A) and (B).

events.what_happened: Bjorn Poonen, 'Hilbert's tenth problem and Mazur's conjecture for large subrings of Q', arXiv math/0306277 (18 June 2003); J. Amer. Math. Soc. 16 (2003), 981-990. Gives infinite sets of primes S (density one possible) for which Hilbert's tenth problem over Z[S^-1] has a negative answer, and for some such S a punctured elliptic curve over Z[S^-1] whose closure in E'(R) has infinitely many connected components. A ring analogue of (B), not Q.
events.revisions: Published in J. Amer. Math. Soc. 16 (2003), 981-990.
events.delivers: Over rings Z[S^-1] for suitable infinite sets S of primes, the finiteness form fails for a punctured elliptic curve. Says nothing about Q, which Mazur's question concerns.

checked_by.who: Journal of the American Mathematical Society (refereed)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper (vol. 16, 2003, pp. 981-990)

events.directly_checkable: The elliptic curve over Z[S^-1] is an explicit object in the paper; its construction was not read.
events.direction: Counter to the ring analogue of (B) over Z[S^-1]. Neutral for Q.
events.object: A punctured elliptic curve E' over Z[S^-1], for an explicit infinite set S of primes, whose closure in E'(R) has infinitely many connected components (per the abstract). Construction not read.

events.what_happened: Kirsten Eisentraeger, Graham Everest and Alexandra Shlapentokh, 'Hilbert's tenth problem and Mazur's conjectures in complementary subrings of number fields', arXiv 1012.4878 (22 December 2010; v2 13 September 2011); Math. Res. Lett. 18 (2011), 1141-1162. For a number field K with a rank-one elliptic curve over K, splits the nonarchimedean primes into disjoint recursive sets, shows Hilbert's tenth problem undecidable on each S-integer ring, and shows that the p-adic and archimedean ring versions of Mazur's conjectures do not hold in these rings.
events.revisions: v2 13 Sep 2011; published in Math. Res. Lett. 18 (2011), 1141-1162.
events.delivers: Ring versions of Mazur's conjectures fail for certain complementary subrings of number fields. Says nothing about Q itself.
events.doubts: Abstract read only; the counterexamples are not described.
events.direction: Counter to the ring versions of Mazur's conjectures for these rings. Analogue only.

events.what_happened: Aleksander Lech Momot, 'Density of rational points on commutative group varieties and small transcendence degree', arXiv 1011.3368 (15 November 2010; v5 25 August 2011). Reformulates and generalises Mazur's problem in transcendence-theoretic terms and states conclusions 'in the direction of' Mazur's conjecture on the topology of rational points, with thirty transcendence corollaries. The abstract states no unconditional closure result over Q.
events.delivers: A reformulation and partial conclusions toward the conjecture, not specified in the abstract. No closure result over Q is stated there.
events.doubts: The conclusions 'in the direction of' the conjecture are not stated in the abstract; the full text was not read.

events.what_happened: Damian Gvirtz, 'Mazur's conjecture and an unexpected rational curve on Kummer surfaces and their superelliptic generalisations', arXiv 1902.02897 (February 2019); Acta Arithmetica 187 (2019), 189-200, DOI 10.4064/aa180201-1-10, online 30 November 2018. Proves special cases of Mazur's conjecture: (i) for a class of elliptic pencils (quadratic twists of the j = 1728 curve E over Q by quartic polynomials), rational points on positive-rank fibres are dense in the real topology; (ii) for the Kummer surface K of a product of two elliptic curves over Q, with no restriction on the j-invariants. The paper states the main conjecture in the union-of-components form, citing Mazur 1992 and 1995.
events.revisions: arXiv 1902.02897 v1 February 2019; the arXiv comments note the published version differs only by a remark acknowledging overlap with Ulas's work. The first public date is the Acta online publication (November 2018), so I use it, though the arXiv posting is later.
events.delivers: Special cases of the union-of-components form (A): positive-rank fibres dense in the real topology for the stated elliptic pencils, and the full statement for the Kummer surface K of E1 x E2 over Q. Does not treat (B), nor general varieties.
events.remains: (A) for general smooth varieties over Q (refuted in general by the 1997 counterexample); (B); (C); (D); (E); (F) beyond the cases proved.
events.directly_checkable: The elliptic pencils and the Kummer surface are explicit; the paper gives explicit equations for the rational curve used. Not checked by me.
events.direction: Consistent with (A) in the cases proved. Does not address (B).
events.object: For (i), the density statement for the elliptic pencils follows from a rational curve on the Kummer surface attached to E x E' over Q, constructed by explicit equations. For (ii), a proof for all Kummer surfaces K of products of two elliptic curves over Q, without j-restriction. Explicit construction.

events.what_happened: Vesselin Dimitrov, Ziyang Gao and Philipp Habegger, 'Uniformity in Mordell-Lang for curves', arXiv 2001.10276 (28 January 2020; v3 31 March 2021); Annals of Mathematics 194 (2021), 237-298. Bounds the rational points on curves of genus at least 2 over number fields by genus, degree and the Mordell-Weil rank of the Jacobian. The abstract says it answers 'in the affirmative a question of Mazur'. Wikipedia lists it under Algebra as 'Mazur's conjecture B'. A different Mazur question (uniform boundedness), not the topology bullet.
events.delivers: Uniform bound on rational points of curves over number fields in terms of genus, degree and rank. A different question from the topology of rational points. Not this problem.
events.remains: All of problem_asks; this is a namesake, recorded so the exclusion is visible.
events.direction: Not about this problem. Its name collision is the reason it appears in the record.

events.what_happened: Rylan Gajek-Leonard, Jeffrey Hatley, Debanjana Kundu and Antonio Lei, 'On a conjecture of Mazur predicting the growth of Mordell-Weil ranks in Z_p-extensions', arXiv 2401.07792 (15 January 2024; v2 15 December 2024). Studies a different Mazur conjecture, on the growth of ranks of elliptic curves over Q in Z_p-extensions of imaginary quadratic fields, with criteria for checking it in examples. No topology of rational points.
events.delivers: Checkable criteria for a different Mazur conjecture. Not this problem.

events.what_happened: Yufan Luo, 'On the Boston's unramified Fontaine-Mazur conjecture', arXiv 2404.18967 (29 April 2024). Partial results on the unramified Fontaine-Mazur conjecture, which is a separate Wikipedia bullet (Number theory) naming Fontaine and Mazur as co-proposers. Mazur's topology of rational points is not mentioned.
events.revisions: A January 2026 follow-up by the same author (arXiv 2601.20395) is reported in a search summary, not opened.
events.delivers: Some basic cases and criteria for an unramified Fontaine-Mazur conjecture; conditional results otherwise. Not this problem.

events.what_happened: Peter Koymans and Carlo Pagano, 'Hilbert's tenth problem via additive combinatorics', arXiv 2412.01768 (2 December 2024; v2 22 April 2025; v3 24 November 2025). Shows Hilbert's tenth problem has a negative answer for every infinite ring finitely generated over Z, including rings of integers of number fields, by constructing elliptic curves without rank growth in quadratic extensions, using full rational 2-torsion, additive combinatorics and 2-descent. Q is not finitely generated over Z, so Q is not covered. The paper's Mazur references are to Mazur-Rubin. Journal status is unverified (a tracker says 'forthcoming in JAMS').
events.delivers: Negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem for all infinite rings finitely generated over Z (rings of integers of number fields included). Does not cover the field Q.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, including Q itself. The paper states no result on (A), (B) or (F).

checked_by.qualification: Survey author on Mazur's work and on Hilbert's tenth problem
checked_by.what_they_did: Reports the result in a 2025 afterword to his survey of Mazur's work, as a negative answer over rings of integers. Reports; does not verify.

events.doubts: Q is outside the stated scope. The result works through elliptic curves with rank stability, not through real topology. No doubts about the result itself were found.
events.direction: Neighbouring problem (Hilbert's tenth problem over finitely generated rings). Does not cut toward or against (A), (B) or (F).

events.what_happened: Levent Alpoge, Manjul Bhargava, Wei Ho and Ari Shnidman, 'Rank stability in quadratic extensions and Hilbert's tenth problem for the ring of integers of a number field', arXiv 2501.18774 (30 January 2025). Shows that for any quadratic extension of number fields K/F there is an abelian variety over F of positive rank whose rank is unchanged over K (Theorem 1.1), and deduces a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over the ring of integers of every number field (Corollary 1.2). Acknowledgements thank Barry Mazur, Adam Morgan, Carlo Pagano and Hector Pasten. A search summary reports publication in Inventiones Mathematicae 243 (2026), 1129-1139 (not verified).
events.revisions: Journal publication reported by a search summary, not verified.
events.delivers: Negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over O_K for every number field K. For K = Q this gives the ring Z, which was already known. Does not give Hilbert's tenth problem over the field Q.
events.remains: Hilbert's tenth problem over Q, and all of problem_asks (A) to (F).

checked_by.qualification: Survey author on Mazur's work and on Hilbert's tenth problem
checked_by.what_they_did: Reports the result in the 2025 afterword to his survey, as a negative answer over rings of integers of number fields. Reports; does not verify.

checked_by.qualification: Journal of record, if the search summary is right
checked_by.what_they_did: Reported as published in Invent. Math. 243 (2026), 1129-1139, DOI 10.1007/s00222-025-01392-3. Not verified against the journal.

events.doubts: Scope: the statement is about rings of integers of number fields. It does not address the field Q, and the authors' own statement covers O_K only.
events.direction: Neighbouring problem. Does not cut toward or against (A), (B) or (F).

events.what_happened: Lior Fishman, David Lambert, Keith Merrill and David Simmons, 'Diophantine approximation on abelian varieties; a conjecture of M. Waldschmidt', arXiv 2506.19060 (23 June 2025). Studies Waldschmidt's density conjecture for simple abelian varieties (the closure of A(K) in A(R) contains A(R)^0). Shows the conjecture for a given simple abelian variety is equivalent to a Diophantine condition on a matrix. For rank-1 elliptic curves over a number field K embedded in R, proves a weak-type Dirichlet theorem, shows it is optimal, and confirms the conjecture in that case. The paper's remark states that for the rank-1 curve LMFDB 110160.cd1 over Q, the closure of A(Q) equals A(R)^0. The text does not mention Mazur.
events.delivers: For rank-1 elliptic curves over number fields K in R (Q included), the closure of E(K) in E(R) contains the identity component E(R)^0. A special case of the abelian-variety part (F), which is not general. Does not treat simple abelian varieties of rank above 1, nor (A) or (B) for general varieties.
events.remains: (F) for higher rank and dimension; (A), (B), (C), (D), (E) for general varieties.
events.doubts: Only an arXiv preprint; no public review found. Competing reading: a search summary states that for genus 1, a rational point set that is infinite is dense in every component of V(R) it meets. The source of that statement was not identified. If it is classical, the rank-1 elliptic case here may not be new, but it would then be a generalisation to number fields in R.
events.direction: Consistent with (A) in the rank-1 elliptic case (the identity component is contained in the closure). A partial result on (F). Does not refute anything.

events.what_happened: On 6 October 2026 OpenAI released 722 mathematical manuscripts (372 result families) at github.com/openai/math, which it said were produced by an 'internal frontier model'. Family 004, 'Hilbert's tenth problem over Q', has a manuscript folder dated 24 September 2026 and claims that no algorithm decides whether a polynomial with integer coefficients has a rational zero (a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over Q). A secondary summary of the manuscript says its reduction 'constructs a sequence of finite rational-solvability tests for integer solvability', using elliptic indices, local comparisons, valuations, height bounds and a compactness argument, and does not mention Mazur or a Diophantine definition of Z over Q. The PDF could not be read through my tools.
events.revisions: Folder dated 2026-09-24; catalogue snapshot 2026-10-06. Secondary reports say three manuscripts were withdrawn within a day for a sign error and fourteen were revised; the catalogue now lists 719. Reports differ on the wording of the statement (integer or rational coefficients).
events.delivers: Claimed, not verified: a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over Q, by a finite-test reduction. On the summary read, it does not establish a Diophantine model of Z in Q. Mazur's Conjecture 3 implies there is none, so a manuscript that did establish one would contradict (B). The summary says this one does not, but I could not read the PDF to check.
events.remains: (A) to (F) are not addressed by this family as far as the summary says. Whether the family is correct is not known.
events.directly_checkable: The manuscript PDF is in the repository. It could not be read through my tools. A third-party Lean project (finitestates/astra-assisted-h10) reportedly checks only the final conditional implication; not opened.
events.doubts: No expert write-up of the Family 004 argument was found. Secondary coverage reports that the IAS advisory group does not endorse the results, that some mathematicians warn the volume exceeds human verification capacity, and that no Lean formalisation of this claim was found. Those are secondary and not checked against OpenAI's page.
events.direction: Claims undecidability of Hilbert's tenth problem over Q. Neighbouring to (B) and (E): a Diophantine model of Z in Q would conflict with (B), but the summary says this family does not use one.

systems.name: an internal frontier model
systems.what_it_did: Per OpenAI's announcement, produced the 722 manuscripts, including the Family 004 claim. The model is internal and unreleased, and no name is given. The Hilbert's tenth problem claim is for a neighbouring problem, not this one.
systems.basis_quote: We're releasing a broad range of new mathematical results produced by an internal frontier model.

ai.disclosed_cost: Per the same announcement as quoted in the forum thread: average compute per result equivalent to roughly three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking with the internal model, across an evaluation of about 4,000 problems.

events.what_happened: On 5 August 2026 Lech Mazur posted a computer-assisted proof of Sendov's conjecture (polynomial zeros and critical points), generated with GPT-5.6 Pro per Wikipedia and formalised in Lean 4 per secondary reports. Terence Tao then published an exposition (dated 12 August 2026 per MathWorld) and extended it to the Phelps-Rodriguez conjecture. Teng Zhang's arXiv 2609.19126 (16 September 2026) builds on it. A namesake: a different problem, with no bearing on rational points or real topology.
events.revisions: Tao's exposition dated 12 Aug 2026 per MathWorld (secondary).

checked_by.qualification: Professor of mathematics (Fields medallist) with expertise in analysis and formalisation
checked_by.what_they_did: Per Wikipedia (secondary), published an exposition verifying and simplifying the argument. Not read directly.

events.doubts: The authors' own write-up (a ProofAtlas PDF cited by Wikipedia) could not be read, so the AI attribution rests on Wikipedia and secondary sites. Those sites disagree on the original date of the conjecture (1958 or 1959; Wikipedia says 1959).
events.direction: Not this problem. Recorded as a namesake.

disputes.summary: Which form of Mazur's conjecture the 1997 counterexample refutes. Poonen's essay and Gvirtz treat the union-of-components form (A) as the refuted one, with the finiteness form (B) still open. A search summary said 'the general form has been refuted' without saying which form. Recorded as a conflict; not resolved here.

The CTSSD counterexample is dated 1997 by the Acta Arithmetica record and Gvirtz's citation. A search summary cited a 1998 paper by the same authors (Invent. Math. 134), which is about the Hasse principle and does not discuss Mazur.

OpenAI's Family 004 is dated 24 September 2026 by its manuscript folder and 6 October 2026 by the release. Secondary reports also disagree on whether the release date was 6 or 7 October (time zone), and on the statement's wording (integer or rational coefficients).
Wikipedia labels the Dimitrov-Gao-Habegger result 'Mazur's conjecture B'; the arXiv abstract says it answers 'a question of Mazur'. Either way it is a different question from the topology bullet.

summary: The frozen Topology bullet reads only 'Mazur's conjectures', with no link; the live page's footnote cites Mazur's 1992 paper 'The topology of rational points' (Experimental Mathematics 1, 1992). The conjectures concern the real topology of closures of rational points of varieties over Q. Conjecture 1 (union of components, restated as openness in 1995) was refuted for smooth surfaces by a 1997 counterexample of Colliot-Thelene, Skorobogatov and Swinnerton-Dyer (Acta Arithmetica 79); Poonen's essay gives the answer as 'no'. Conjecture 3 (finitely many components) is still listed as open, with little progress beyond Mazur's own special cases, in Poonen's essay with its 2025 afterword. Both points were read from secondary sources, because the 1992, 1995, 1997 and 1999 PDFs could not be read through my tools. Since 26 January 2024 I found no event that settles or refutes Conjecture 3, or the consequence that Z is not diophantine in Q. The post-window events that touch the problem are: (i) Fishman, Lambert, Merrill and Simmons (arXiv 2506.19060, June 2025), which confirms Waldschmidt's abelian-variety density for rank-1 elliptic curves over number fields in R, including Q, a special case of the abelian part (F), though their text does not mention Mazur; (ii) two results on Hilbert's tenth problem over rings of integers (Koymans and Pagano, December 2024; Alpoge, Bhargava, Ho and Shnidman, January 2025), which do not cover the field Q and do not address the topology question; (iii) OpenAI's 6 October 2026 release of 722 manuscripts from an 'internal frontier model', whose Family 004 claims a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over Q. By a secondary summary, its reduction uses finite rational-solvability tests and does not go through a Diophantine model of Z in Q or mention Mazur. The PDF could not be read, no expert write-up was found, and the claim is unverified. The namesake events are recorded as different questions: Dimitrov-Gao-Habegger (2020), Gajek-Leonard et al. (January 2024), Luo (April 2024), and Lech Mazur's Sendov proof (August 2026, with GPT-5.6 Pro named by Wikipedia). AI: no system was found in any source on the topology conjectures. The AI-credited items are the OpenAI family (a neighbouring problem, with the system named only as 'an internal frontier model') and the Sendov namesake. For the Sendov namesake I could not read the authors' write-up, so no system is recorded in ai.systems. Close calls: (a) which conjecture the 1997 counterexample refutes; (b) whether the 2025 rank-1 result is new, since a search summary asserts a classical genus-1 density statement from an unidentified source; (c) whether the OpenAI family touches the Mazur chain, which depends on the PDF.
competing_reading: Read 'Mazur's conjectures' as the whole 1992 programme, not only Conjecture 1 and 3. On that reading, part (F), the abelian-variety density question, is a plural part of the bullet, and the 2025 Fishman et al. result is a real movement on it. It is only a rank-1 elliptic case over fields in R, and may be classical for genus 1 (per an unsourced search summary). Alternatively read the OpenAI family as moving the Mazur chain: a Diophantine model of Z in Q would contradict Conjecture 3, so a manuscript establishing one would be a major event. The summary says Family 004 does not use one, but I could not read the PDF to confirm.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The 1992 paper's text, for the numbering of Conjectures 1 to 4, the homotopy-type statement, and the abelian-variety statement. (2) The 1997 Acta paper, to see which form the surface refutes and whether its closure has finitely many components. (3) The Fishman et al. introduction, to see whether they treat the rank-1 case as a case of Mazur's abelian question and whether the genus-1 density statement is classical. (4) The OpenAI Family 004 manuscript (main.pdf) and the repository's CONTENTS, to check for any Diophantine model of Z in Q, any mention of Mazur, and what the internal model contributed. (5) Expert reports on Family 004 and on the Sendov proof. (6) Mazur's 1995 update, to confirm the open-subset form.

incomplete: (1) The 1992 paper and the 1995 update were not readable, so Conjectures 2 and 4, the homotopy-type statement and the abelian-variety statement are taken from secondary citations; their numbering and exact wording are unverified. (2) The 1997 CTSSD Acta paper was not read; the refuted form and the 'finitely many components remains open' status rest on Poonen's essay, Gvirtz and Cornelissen-Zahidi. (3) Waldschmidt 1999 was not read; its rank threshold comes from search summaries. (4) The OpenAI Family 004 manuscript and the repository's CONTENTS list could not be read; I did not check whether any other family in the 722 bears on Mazur's conjectures, so the AI search for this problem is incomplete at manuscript level. The OpenAI statement is taken from a forum thread that quotes the release, and OpenAI's own page was not opened. (5) The Sendov namesake's authors' write-up could not be read; its AI attribution rests on Wikipedia and secondary sites. (6) Full text was read for Koymans-Pagano, ABHS, Fishman et al., Gvirtz, and the Cornelissen-Zahidi acknowledgements; for other events only the abstract or extracted statements were read, so AI disclosure in their full text was not checked. (7) Journal publication of Koymans-Pagano and ABHS is reported by a tracker and a search summary, not verified. (8) Items reported only in search summaries and not opened, so not recorded as events: Munshi (Mazur's question for quadratic and cubic elliptic pencils, a claimed affirmative answer); Rohrlich and Kuwata-Wang (earlier elliptic pencil cases); Zhizhong Huang (unconditional density for K3 surfaces of Cassels-Schinzel type; date unknown); the isotrivial elliptic surfaces paper arXiv 0911.3881; Pheidas's proposed approach; Lue Pan and Calegari (Fontaine-Mazur, namesake); Luo's January 2026 follow-up; Eisentraeger-Everest-Shlapentokh-type 2025 undecidability work; Garcia-Fritz, Pasten and Vidaux 2024; Konigsmann on a universal definition of Z in Q; Pagano-Shlapentokh 2025 talk on defining Q with one universal quantifier; Shlapentokh's 2006 book chapter; and the Gvirtz-Chen and Kuhne results mentioned in summaries. Munshi and Huang may bear directly on the elliptic-pencil cases and are the most important gap. (9) No arXiv listing or journal search was possible beyond search-engine results and the author page, so a 2024-2026 paper that never surfaced in these searches could be missing. (10) The 2025 claim of a classical genus-1 density result (search summary, unsourced) was not checked.
